aisec: AI-assisted offensive tooling is hitting core security infrastructure: Check Point management servers and Palo Alto firewalls were compromised, while an Anthropic scanner-found Drupal flaw is now exploited.
Agentic attack frameworks are spreading: Microsoft says ARTEX is used by Chinese and North Korean groups, while Cisco Talos and Swiss and Italian agencies warn of autonomous AI-driven attacks.
Research targets AI system security itself, covering agent auditing, model-as-a-service assurance, LLM watermarks, Rowhammer backdoors, deception defenses, and privacy and poisoning risks.
ai: AI-driven attacks dominate coverage, with insurers noting a divide between organizations with and without AI defenses, and incident trackers cataloguing real-world AI-enhanced hacking.
Agent and platform competition continues: Amazon and Meta reportedly discuss lifting Amazon's roughly two-month block on Meta's Muse shopping agent.
Infrastructure and governance pressure persists: AI data centers are harder to build, Nvidia faces scrutiny over Megaspeed chips, and a former OpenAI employee accused of bugging offices got bail.
cyber: Critical flaws are under active exploitation: Drupal RCE (Fail2Install, CISA KEV listed), GeoServer chains, and a CVSS 10.0 Hex.pm bug that compromised six registry servers.
Supply-chain attacks continue through backdoored WordPress plugins, malicious NuGet packages aimed at .NET developers, and third-party components in network appliances.
Breaches and access abuse include a FinCEN intrusion, a reported CIA analysis system breach, and vishing-driven cloud account takeovers, plus Microsoft November update authentication issues.
